verse: The way of the slothful is like a hedge of thorns. The way of the just is without offense. (Pro 15:19)
The intentions of the robust continually bring forth abundance. But all the lazy are continually in need. (Pro 21:5)
Go to the ant, you lazy person; watch its ways and be wise. Without having any chief or overseer or ruler, it prepares its food in summertime and gathers its supplies in harvest. (Pro 6:6-8)
How long will you slumber, you lazy one? When will you rise up from your sleep? (Pro 6:9)
You will sleep a little, you will slumber a little, you will fold your hands a little to sleep, and then destitution will meet with you, like a traveler, and poverty, like an armed man. (Pro 6:10)
Do not love sleep, or you will come to poverty. Open your eyes and you will have plenty to eat. (Pro 20:13)
Whoever works his land will have plenty to eat. But whoever continually pursues worthless things is most foolish. (Pro 12:11)
The neglectful hand makes one poor. But the hand of the diligent brings riches. (Pro 10:4)
In all hard work, there shall be abundance. But where there are many words, there is often need. (Pro 14:23)
Like vinegar to the teeth, and smoke to the eyes, so are the lazy to those who employ them. (Pro 10:26)
The lazy man does not roast that which he took in hunting: but the substance of a diligent man is precious. (Pro 12:27)
In idleness there is loss and great poverty, because idleness is the mother of hunger and famine. (Tob 4:13)
Laziness sends one into a deep sleep, and an idle person will go hungry. (Pro 19:15)
In the morning plant your seed, and in the evening let not your hand rest, for you do not know which will prosper, whether one or the other, or if both of them will be equally good. (Eccl 11:6)
The lazy man is like a dirty stone, and all will speak about his disgrace. (Sir 22:1)
The lazy man is like a lump of dung, and all who touch him will shake of their hands. (Sir 22:2)

We command you, believers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from believers who live in idleness and not according to the tradition that they received from us. For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we did not live in idleness among you; nor did we eat anyone’s bread without paying for it but worked night and day with labor and hardship so that we would not be a burden to any of you. (2 Thes 3:6-8)
Do not be impudent in your speech, or lazy and slack in your deeds. (Sir 4:29)
Whoever is faithful with very little is faithful also in much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much. (Luk 16:10)
Whoever works his land shall be satisfied with bread. But whoever chases worthless pursuits will be filled with need. (Pro 28:19)

Woe to you who rise up in the morning to pursue drunkenness, and to drink even until evening, so as to be inflamed with wine. Harp and lyre and timbrel and pipe, as well as wine, are at your feasts. But you do not respect the work of the Lord, nor do you consider the works of his hands. Because of this, my people have been led away as captives, for they did not have knowledge, and their nobles have passed away from famine, and their multitudes have dried up from thirst. (Is 5:11-13)
The lazy one craves and gets nothing. But the soul of he who labors is richly supplied. (Pro 13:4)
Whoever is dissolute and slack in his work is the brother of him who destroys his own works. (Pro 18:9)
Desires kill the lazy, for his hands are not willing to work at all. (Pro 21:25)

I passed by the field of a lazy man, and by the vineyard of a foolish man, and behold, it was entirely filled with nettles, and thorns had covered its surface, and the stonewall was destroyed. (Pro 24:30-31)

He who had received one talent, approaching, said: ‘Lord, I know that you are a hard man. You reap where you have not sown and gather where you have not scattered. And so, being afraid, I went out and hid your talent in the earth. Behold, you have what is yours.’ But his lord said to him in response: ‘You evil and lazy servant! You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered.’ (Matt 25:24-26)
The lazy one was not willing to plough in season. Therefore, when harvest comes, there will be nothing. (Pro 20:4)
I will refresh the weary and replenish all who are faint. (Jer 31:25)
The Lord God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it. (Gen 2:15)
Let everything that you do, whether in word or in deed, be done all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God the Father through him. (Col 3:17)

While we were with you, we insisted on this to you: that if anyone was not willing to work, neither should he eat. For we have heard that there are some among you who act disruptively, not working at all, but eagerly meddling. Now we charge those who act in this way, and we beg them in the Lord Jesus Christ, that they work in silence and eat their own bread. (2 Thes 3:10-12)
Whatever you do, do it from the heart, as for the Lord, and not for men. For you know that you will receive from the Lord the repayment of an inheritance. (Col 3:23-24)
Therefore, whether you eat or drink, or whatever else you may do, do everything for the glory of God. (1 Cor 10:31)
Accomplish your work in good time. And God will give you your reward in his time. (Sir 51:30)
See to it that you walk cautiously, not like the foolish, but like the wise: making the most of the time, because the days are evil. (Eph 5:15-16)
You should not hate laborious works, nor the rustic life created by the Most High. (Sir 7:15)

Do everything without murmuring or disputing. So may you be without blame, innocent children of God, without reproof, in the midst of a depraved and perverse nation, among whom you shine like lights in the world. (Phil 2:14-16)

Aspire to lead a quiet life and carry out your business and do your work with your own hands, just as we have instructed you, and walk honestly with those who are outside, and be dependent on no one. (1 Thes 4:10-12)
Whatever your hand is able to do, do it earnestly. (Eccl 9:10)
The Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation; He is my God, and I will praise him, my father's God, and I will exalt him. (Exo 15:2)
God, the Lord, is my strength; he makes my feet like the deer's; he makes me tread on high places. (Hab 3:19)
Seek the Lord and his strength; seek his presence continually! (1 Chron 16:11)
My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever. (Ps 73:26)
I pray that, he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened in the inner being with power through his Spirit. (Eph 3:16)
Be strong in the Lord, and in the strength of the Lord’s power. (Eph 6:10)
The Lord is my strength and my shield. My heart trusts in him, and I am helped. Therefore, my heart rejoices, and with my song I will praise him. (Ps 28:7)
Now to him who is able to do abundantly far more than all we can ask or imagine, by the power that is at work within us. (Eph 3:20)

It is he that gives power to the weary and strengthens them that are powerless. Youths shall faint, and labor, and young men shall fall exhausted. But those who wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength, they shall take wings as eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint. (Is 40:29-31)
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me. (Phil 4:13)
The Lord your God is with you; a warrior who gives you victory. The Lord will take delight in you, and in his love he will renew you. (Zeph 3:17)
